title: The Other Station
story:
Ingrid, on the handheld radio, voice thin against the wind:

"Engineer, the hut at Skua Ridge keeps a second Docker engine as our fallback. When we need it, it will be midnight and somebody will be typing endpoints from memory. I don't want that. Give the hut a name the CLI understands, and prove the name works by starting a probe container there. The cable isn't laid yet, so for now point it at the endpoint in `/workspace/hut-endpoint.txt`. Over."
objectives: Create a context named `backup-station` for the endpoint in `/workspace/hut-endpoint.txt`, with the description `Backup hut engine`
Make `backup-station` the active context with `docker context use`
Through that context, run a detached `hut-probe` container from `alpine:3.20` that sleeps (`sleep infinity`)
startingState: Only the `default` context exists. The file `/workspace/hut-endpoint.txt` holds the endpoint to use.
hints: The Docker CLI can talk to several engines. A context bundles an endpoint with a name, so switching engines is one short command instead of environment variables or long flags.
Create it with `docker context create NAME --docker host=ENDPOINT --description TEXT`, then switch to it with `docker context use NAME`. `docker context ls` marks the active one with an asterisk.

```bash
docker context create backup-station \
  --docker host=$(cat hut-endpoint.txt) \
  --description "Backup hut engine"
docker context use backup-station
docker context show
docker run -d --name hut-probe alpine:3.20 sleep infinity
```

validation.description: A context `backup-station` exists and points at `unix:///var/run/docker.sock`
The context `backup-station` has the description `Backup hut engine`
`backup-station` is the active context (`docker context use backup-station`)

solution: docker context create backup-station --docker host=unix:///var/run/docker.sock --description 'Backup hut engine'
docker run -d --name hut-probe alpine:3.20 sleep infinity
debrief: Switching engines is now one word instead of a remembered socket path: the context bundles endpoint and description under a name. Pro tip: `docker --context NAME ps` runs a single command elsewhere without changing the active context.
